question: By an external point P, two tangents are drawn to a circle, touching the circle at points A and B. The chord of contact AB subtends an angle θ at the center of the circle O. What is the angle ∠APB between the tangents in terms of θ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, the angle between two tangents drawn from an external point and the angle subtended by their chord of contact at the center are supplementary.

The sum of these two angles is exactly 180°.

∠APB + ∠AOB = 180°

∠APB = 180° − θ

**∴ The correct answer is 180° − θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle subtended by the chord of contact AB at the center O = ∠AOB = θ

**Method:**

⇒ A radius is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.

⇒ ∠OAP = 90° (Since OA is a radius and PA is a tangent)

⇒ ∠OBP = 90° (Since OB is a radius and PB is a tangent)

⇒ In quadrilateral OAPB, the sum of all interior angles is 360°.

⇒ ∠OAP + ∠OBP + ∠AOB + ∠APB = 360°

⇒ 90° + 90° + θ + ∠APB = 360°

⇒ 180° + θ + ∠APB = 360°

⇒ ∠APB = 360° − 180° − θ

⇒ ∠APB = 180° − θ

**∴ The correct answer is 180° − θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

Since the opposite angles ∠OAP and ∠OBP sum to 180°, the quadrilateral OAPB is cyclic. This means points O, A, P, and B lie on a single circle where the line segment OP acts as its diameter.

Lengths of Tangents

Tangents drawn from a single external point to a circle are always equal in length. Therefore, the tangent segment PA equals tangent segment PB.

Angle Subtended by Arc

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of the circle is exactly double the angle it subtends at any other point on the remaining part of the circle.
